title: Organising writing: paragraphs, linking words and sentence variety
canonical_examples_source: Language rules self-verified; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS).

blocks.content: Good writing is not just correct — it is organised. Paragraphs, linking words and a mix of sentences guide the reader smoothly through your ideas.
Group sentences about one idea into a paragraph, and start a new paragraph when you move to a new idea.

steps: Paragraph 1 tells about the morning of the trip.
When the writer reaches the beach, a NEW idea begins.

blocks.question: When should you start a new paragraph?
options: when you move to a new idea
blocks.explain: A new paragraph signals a new idea, so start one when the idea changes.
blocks.rule: Group sentences about one idea into a paragraph; start a new paragraph for a new idea.

practiceItems.prompt: a paragraph should hold one main ___
start a new paragraph for a new ___
sentences in a paragraph should be about the ___ idea (same/different)
a group of sentences about one idea is called a ___

blocks.content: Linking words join ideas smoothly: also (to add), so (to show a result), however (to contrast), then (for time order).

blocks.prompt: Choose a linking word that adds more: I like mango. ___, I like plum.
blocks.explain: 'also' adds another idea of the same kind.
blocks.rule: Linking words join ideas: also to add, so for a result, however to contrast, then for time order.

practiceItems.prompt: linking word to add another idea
linking word to show a result
linking word to contrast two ideas
linking word to show time order

blocks.question: A paragraph jumps from breakfast, to space rockets, to new shoes. What is the problem?
options: The sentences are not about one topic — a paragraph should stick to one main idea
blocks.explain: A good paragraph sticks to one main idea, with each sentence connected to it. Jumping between unrelated topics leaves the reader lost. This is about coherence — keeping the writing on one track.
blocks.rule: Keep a paragraph to one main idea, with sentences linked to it.
blocks.principle: Coherent writing stays on one topic and connects its ideas.
canonical_solution: A paragraph needs one main idea
Its sentences should connect to that idea
So the problem is a lack of coherence

rubric.look_for: checks whether the sentences share a topic
explains a paragraph keeps one main idea

misconceptions.coach: The issue is the mixed topics, not the length.
Unrelated sentences make the paragraph hard to follow.

blocks.content: One idea per paragraph, linking words to connect them, and a mix of short and long sentences — that is well-organised writing. Let's practise!
